keywords: what is simpler,simpler is,about simpler,infrastructure,simpler acronym,simpler full name,simpler background,stand for
answer: SIMPLER stands for Swedish Infrastructure for Medical Population-Based Life-Course and Environmental Research. It provides national and international researchers with data for research about dietary and lifestyle factors, genetics, and how they affect health — particularly in later life. Two cohorts form the basis: the Swedish Mammography Cohort (SMC) and the Cohort of Swedish Men (COSM), with approximately 107,000 participants in total. Contact: simpler@surgsci.uu.se

keywords: smc,mammography,swedish mammography cohort,swedish mammography,women cohort,female cohort,smc women,smc baseline,smc response rate,women born
answer: The Swedish Mammography Cohort (SMC) includes women born 1914–1948 (aged 38–76) living in Uppsala and Västmanland counties, invited through the mammography screening programme in 1987–1990. Of 90,303 invited, 66,651 responded (74%); 61,433 remained after exclusions.\nIn 2019, 19,081 women completed the health questionnaire and 14,922 the lifestyle questionnaire.\nClinical subcohorts: SMCC Uppsala (from 2003; 5,341 women in cycle 1) and SMCC Västmanland in Västerås (from 2010; 2,705 women in cycle 1).

keywords: cosm,cohort of swedish men,men cohort,male cohort,cosm men,cosm baseline,cosm response rate,men born,cosm 1997
answer: The Cohort of Swedish Men (COSM) was formed in 1997 from men born 1918–1952 (aged 45–79) living in Västmanland and Örebro counties. Of 100,303 invited, 48,850 responded (49%); 45,906 remained after exclusions.\nIn 2019, 18,901 men completed the health questionnaire and 16,166 the lifestyle questionnaire.\nClinical subcohorts: COSMC in Västerås (cycle 1 2010–2017; 4,773 men) and one in Örebro (N=232, started 2014, ongoing).

FFQ stands for Food Frequency Questionnaire, part of the lifestyle questionnaires. Available FFQs:

• FFQ2009 — both sexes: 149 items, past year

• HQ2008 — 30,621 women and 29,503 men
• HQ2019 — 19,081 women and 18,901 men

answer:
The Explore Variable tab lets you browse the variables in each dataset and build a list of the variables you want to request:
1. Pick one or more datasets in the Datasets dropdown (clicking a group name selects the whole group)
2. Click Explore variable: one sub-tab per dataset appears

answer:
The Table tab creates descriptive summary tables:
1. Optionally choose Stratify by to split the results by a variable; leave No stratification to summarise the whole cohort
2. Select one or more Variables (required)
3. Click Run table
4. The table shows counts and percentages for each selected variable (for each group if you stratified)

answer:
The Combination Plot tab draws UpSet plots to show how many participants share combinations of variables:

answer:
To apply for SIMPLER data:
1. Applications are submitted electronically via iLab: https://uu.ilab.agilent.com/service_center/show_external/3659

This app uses an anonymized version of the SIMPLER dataset:
• A subset of participants has been removed so that any combination of variables contains at least 10 individuals; the exact number is shown on the Homepage and in the note above tables and plots
• Values for breast cancer among male participants have been set to NA
• Baseline age was dichotomized as ≤60 vs >60 years, and BMI (self-reported and measured) as <25 vs ≥25 kg/m2
• Numbers are therefore approximate and meant for orientation when preparing a research proposal
• The app collects only anonymous usage statistics (visits, events, country-level geography) — no personal data is stored

Health examination in the subcohorts (after overnight fasting, by a research nurse):

answer:
SIMPLER biorepository:
• Blood and adipose tissue collected in the morning after overnight fasting; stool and first-morning urine collected at home
• Types: EDTA, lithium-heparin and citrate plasma, serum, buffy coat, urine, adipose tissue, stool
• Samples protected from light, aliquoted into 500 µl cryotubes and frozen within 45 min
• Storage: −80 °C (2003–2023), −70 °C since 2023; DNA at −20 °C
• ~40,000 saliva DNA samples (8,500 women + 31,500 men) and ~13,000 blood DNA samples
• ~602 incident urological cancer cases with samples (Örebro University Hospital)
• Total: over 800,000 samples

keywords: limitations,limitation,bias,representative,representativeness,generalizability,generalisability,measurement error,weaknesses,selection bias
answer:
Main limitations to consider:
• Representativeness: both cohorts resembled the Swedish population in 1997 (age, BMI, education, smoking); this matters more for disease occurrence than for risk factor–disease associations
• Initial response: 74% in SMC, 49% in COSM
• A common 1997 baseline means follow-up data for women
• FFQs carry random and systematic error, and the number of food items changed between questionnaires, so combine them carefully
• Participants were not re-contacted to clarify ambiguous answers
• Subcohort size was limited by funding

keywords: diet,dietary intake,nutrient,nutrient database,energy intake,energy adjusted,portion size,validation,validity,reproducibility,physical activity,exercise
answer: Diet: nutrient and energy intakes are estimated from FFQ frequencies and sex- and age-specific portion sizes, using Swedish Food Agency databases. The diet database has total energy and 51 nutrients, as absolute and energy-adjusted (residual method) values; implausible energy intakes (±3 SD) are excluded from energy-adjusted analyses.\nValidity vs 24-h recalls: mean r = 0.65 for macronutrients, 0.49 for micronutrients; test–retest ICC 0.54–0.85.\nPhysical activity: seven questions; the exercise question correlated 0.64 with activity records and 0.38 with accelerometers.

• One-day food record (from 2010)
• Toilet habit questionnaire with the Bristol stool scale (from 2013)
The final lifestyle questionnaire was also used for the main cohorts in 2009 and 2019.
